jump.name: the jump
jump.title: How to record your jump
jump.lead: A countermovement vertical jump: you dip, drive up with your arms and land in the same spot.
execution: Start standing still for a second, side-on to the camera.
Dip quickly bending knees and hips, and swing your arms back.
Jump as high as you can, swinging your arms up.
Land on the balls of your feet and absorb by bending your knees.
You can do several jumps in the same video, with a short pause between them.
mistakes: Leaving the frame during flight: leave room above your head.
Turning your body toward the camera when landing.
Recording in slow motion or with a filter that crops the video.

squat.name: the squat
squat.title: How to record your squat
squat.lead: A bodyweight squat: you lower with control to a comfortable depth and stand back up.
execution: Feet hip-width apart and arms forward for balance.
Lower by pushing your hips back, chest up.
Go as deep as you can without lifting your heels.
Stand up without bouncing and repeat at a steady pace.
mistakes: Facing the camera: from the front it can't see how much the knee bends.
Someone else crossing the frame during the set.
Cutting the video before the last rep is up.

styleGuide.metaDescription: Living instrument: KinesiApp's visual identity, with its palette, type, components, charts and sample screens.
styleGuide.title: Living instrument
styleGuide.lead: KinesiApp reads like a measuring instrument that breathes: every joint has its color, every range its zone, and every figure reaches its value with the inertia of a real needle.
styleGuide.sampleNote: Figures are sample data from a 40-second squat set.
styleGuide.home: Go to the top of the guide

hero.skeleton: Side-view skeleton doing a squat, with the knee, trunk, hip and center of gravity in their colors

color.lead: Color never decorates: it says what is being measured. The same four signals paint the skeleton, the lines and the needles; zones tell whether a measure fell short, hit the target or went past it, and risk has its own scale with a word and steps.
color.signalsLead: One per joint or measure, the same in every view.
color.zonesLead: Relative to the risk-free knee flexion range the AI used for each analysis; in the sample squat, {range}.
color.riskLead: Always shown with the word and one to three steps: it never depends on color alone.
color.shared: Cobalt is both the knee and the main action: the knee is the app's leading measure, and buttons never appear inside a chart, so they don't get mixed up.

type.lead: A narrow, technical display face for figures and headings, and a warm, legible sans for everything else. Figures are tabular so they don't jump while counting.
type.displayUse: Display and figures: headings, gauge readings and metrics.
type.sansUse: Text: paragraphs, controls, labels and notices.
type.sampleBody: On the fifth repetition your trunk leaned more than usual; check the chart to see at which second it happened.

glyphs.lead: The same thin-stroke, round-cap set from the first design. They go with the text, never replace it.
